sources.title: Dezso, Griffiths and Bastiawan, Charter of Pucangan (1041), DHARMA edition and translation
sources.note: Direct scholarly edition checked at the metadata, Sanskrit verses 13 to 15, Old Javanese face B lines 1 to 4, translation paragraphs 13 to 15, and date note 26. Scope: The 1041 royal charter is retrospective and rhetorically modeled; it securely witnesses its own date, languages, script, and royal claims, not every detail of the 1016 destruction or ordinary life.

sources.title: Bastiawan, Sofianto, Jaelani and Griffiths, When, Where, and What Were Janggala and Kadiri?
sources.note: Publisher abstract and indexed Periodisation and territory discussion checked for the changing uses of Janggala and Kadiri and the problem of treating 1042 as a clean permanent border. Scope: Used to preserve current scholarly uncertainty; it does not certify the atlas polygon or a single exact partition line.

sources.title: Arjunawiwaha: The Marriage of Arjuna of Mpu Kanwa, Brill introduction
sources.note: Scholarly introduction checked for Airlangga, the 1041 Pucangan inscription, the Arjunawiwaha court context, retirement, and remembered division. Scope: Court biography and literary patronage are distinguished from a complete social history or precise political map.

sources.title: P. E. de Josselin de Jong, The Character of the Hindu-Javanese State
sources.note: Peer-reviewed state-history synthesis checked for Airlangga's succession, Kadiri or Panjalu, Singhasari, and the limits of later narrative sources. Scope: Used for broad political sequence only, not to turn court ideology into uniform administration or borders.

sources.title: Lydia Kieven, Following the Cap-Figure in Majapahit Temple Reliefs
sources.note: Scholarly political outline checked for the Airlangga division, Panjalu or Kediri, the 1222 transition, and Singhasari chronology. Scope: A later art-history synthesis is used as a chronological cross-check, not as eyewitness evidence.

sources.title: Berguru Pada Leluhur, Direktorat Warisan dan Diplomasi Budaya
sources.note: Official cultural-history discussion checked for the 1037 Kamalagyan or Wringin Sapta dam, Brantas flooding, boat traffic, fields, and water officials. Scope: The named project is not generalized into complete regional flood control or household water supply.

sources.title: Beberapa Prasasti yang Berisi tentang Irigasi Sawah, Direktorat Pelindungan Kebudayaan
sources.note: Official epigraphic survey checked for Old Javanese terms and examples concerning dams, dikes, reservoirs, tunnels, channels, fields, and water-related officials. Scope: Infrastructure terms and named works do not prove identical systems in every settlement.

sources.title: Titi Surti Nastiti, Perkembangan Aksara Kwadrat di Jawa Tengah, Jawa Timur, dan Bali
sources.note: Official peer-reviewed epigraphic study checked for Hantang stone D 9, Jayabhaya, 1057 Saka or 1135 CE, quadrate script, and the phrase panjalu jayati. Scope: A royal victory formula does not reveal the campaign, casualties, spoken language, or general literacy.

sources.title: Gapura Plumbangan dan Sejarahnya, Balai Pelestarian Kebudayaan Wilayah XI
sources.note: Official heritage account checked for the 1120 Panumbangan inscription, Bameswara, and the sima grant, while distinguishing the later gateway. Scope: One charter records a selected locality and cannot supply a kingdom-wide tax schedule.

sources.title: Situs Besole: Sisa-sisa Kerajaan Kadiri, Berkala Arkeologi
sources.note: Official archaeological journal study checked for Kadiri inscriptions, ruler sequence, Daha, and cautiously attributed brick remains. Scope: Site attribution and incomplete inscription sequences remain qualified.

sources.title: Prasasti, Direktorat Pelindungan Kebudayaan
sources.note: Official explanation checked for inscriptions as formal legal and sacred records on stone, copper, and other media. Scope: Document function is not confused with the survival rate or ordinary literacy.

sources.title: Prasasti dan Citralekha, Balai Pelestarian Cagar Budaya Yogyakarta
sources.note: Official account checked for specialized inscription writers, Old Javanese language and script knowledge, court formulae, and administrative skill. Scope: Specialist literacy is not treated as universal schooling.

sources.title: The Figure of the Tanda in Old Javanese Literary and Epigraphic Records
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparison checked for the elite guard or warrior title in epigraphic and literary evidence from Kediri onward. Scope: A title is not expanded into a complete army organization or a literal reading of poetic combat.

sources.title: In Search of Lost Time: The Pandawa Story in the Javanese Cultural Tradition
sources.note: University research checked for Jayabhaya's court, the 1157 Bharatayuddha, Mpu Sedah and Mpu Panuluh, performance, and creative Old Javanese adaptation. Scope: Court literature is not treated as a census of audiences or exact reportage.

sources.title: Helen Creese, The Balinese Kakawin Tradition
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology checked for East Javanese kakawin, poets and patrons, later Balinese manuscript transmission, and performance contexts. Scope: Composition, recopying, and the age of a surviving manuscript are kept distinct.

sources.title: Traces of Salyawadha in the Old Javanese Bharatayuddha and Balinese Literature
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study checked for the 1157 Bharatayuddha and later textual adaptation in Bali. Scope: Later copies and adaptations do not become twelfth-century physical artifacts.

sources.title: Mengenal Cerita Panji, Direktorat Warisan dan Diplomasi Budaya
sources.note: Official cultural-history discussion checked for Panjalu or Daha, Janggala, and the later regional spread and many versions of Panji stories. Scope: Panji characters are not treated as straightforward biographies of one historical prince and princess.

sources.title: Candi Panataran: Candi Kerajaan Masa Majapahit
sources.note: Archaeological study checked for the 1197 Srnga Palah inscription and the mostly later Majapahit building phases. Scope: The early sacred place is not used to backdate the entire surviving complex.

sources.title: Tondowongso: Menyingkap Peradaban Kediri, Kementerian Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan
sources.note: Official archaeological monograph checked for the brick sanctuary, eleventh- to thirteenth-century horizon, layout, objects, and excavation limits. Scope: A ritual complex is not used as an ordinary-house plan, toilet plan, or precise royal chronology.

sources.title: Arca-arca dari Situs Tondowongso dan Gurah, Berkala Arkeologi
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological study checked for Brahma, Candra, Surya, Nandi, yoni, materials, and unfinished research. Scope: Finds from a sacred complex do not establish uniform belief or craft access.

sources.title: Lesley Pullen, Kediri and Singhasari: Stone Sculpture from the Eleventh to the Fourteenth Century
sources.note: Cambridge chapter summary checked for sparse securely attributed Kediri sculpture, Singhasari works under Kertanagara, textile patterns, and interregional trade context. Scope: Style and pattern comparisons are not made into exact trade itineraries or universal clothing.

sources.title: Ninie Susanti, Rajendra Chola's Invasion and the Rise of Airlangga
sources.note: Cambridge and ISEAS chapter summary checked for the sea route from China through Malacca and Indonesian waters to India and the western Indian Ocean, and for Indian Ocean port growth. Scope: The regional route establishes an Indian Ocean connection, not a specific itinerary, cargo, merchant identity, or East Javanese court's control of every port.

sources.title: Zhao Rugua, Zhufan zhi, translated by Hirth and Rockhill
sources.note: Cornell scan checked at the Java account for crops, animals, salt, trade goods, merchants, clothing, government, and healing. Scope: This thirteenth-century Chinese compilation describes Java broadly through mediated information; it is not an East Java census or household diary.

sources.title: The Lingwai Daida of Zhou Qufei: A Translation and Critical Edition
sources.note: University-hosted annotated translation checked for the 1178 Java account, dwellings, officials, amusements, trade, and information obtained through traders, sailors, and older texts. Scope: Vivid outsider reporting is labeled regional and mediated rather than universal.

sources.title: Judith H. Maxwell, Texts and Textiles in Medieval Java
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis checked for textiles as labor, gifts, payments, trade goods, literary images, and epigraphic evidence. Scope: Elite gifts and sculpted patterns do not define every person's clothes.

sources.title: Helen Creese, Subhadrawiwaha: an Old Javanese kakawin
sources.note: University thesis checked for marriage forms and ceremonies discussed across Old Javanese kakawin. Scope: The particular poem is later than this atlas period, so it supports cautious literary themes rather than direct household statistics.

sources.title: Alnoza and Sulistyowati, Konstruksi Masyarakat Jawa Kuno terhadap Transgender Perempuan, AMERTA
sources.note: Peer-reviewed epigraphic tables checked for Padlegan I and Kemulan occupational categories, sima administration, and the walyan healer term. Scope: Named occupational categories do not reveal treatment recipes, household prevalence, or every person's fixed identity.

sources.title: Cakrawala Mandala Dwipantara: Wawasan Kemaritiman Kerajaan Singhasari
sources.note: Official archaeology and cultural-history essay checked for Singhasari's 1222 to 1292 frame, Kertanagara, later maritime policy, and limited material evidence. Scope: Later chronicle intrigue is not treated as secure eyewitness history, and post-1279 expeditions are outside the card's interval.

sources.title: Environment, Trade and Society in Southeast Asia: A Longue Duree Perspective
sources.note: Scholarly volume section checked for late Mataram in East Java, the 1016 attack as remembered by Pucangan, Airlangga's restoration, and subsequent political division. Scope: Used only as broad overview context; its regional reconstruction does not validate the atlas polygon or erase chronological debate.

sources.title: S. O. Robson, Java at the Crossroads: Aspects of Javanese Cultural History in the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Centuries
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis checked for the geographic distinction among Kadiri, Janggala, Singhasari, the upper and lower Brantas, and political continuity. Scope: Used as a broad orientation source, not proof that one state controlled the atlas's multi-island polygon.

sources.title: Robert Wessing, A Tiger in the Heart: The Javanese Rampok Macan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed historical framing checked for Kediri as an heir to Airlangga's Kahuripan, its endpoint in 1222, and succession by Singhasari or Tumapel from 1222 to 1292. Scope: Used only for the overview's broad political chronology and the arithmetic of the atlas's 57-year lag; the article's later tiger-ritual argument is outside this card's evidence.

sources.title: Thomas M. Hunter, The Body of the King: Reappraising Singhasari Period Syncretism
sources.note: Journal abstract and source discussion checked for conflicting Singhasari records, court and priestly perspectives, Mula Malurung evidence, and Kertanagara's politico-religious program. Scope: Contradictory textual traditions are kept visible rather than fused into one seamless narrative.

sources.title: Candi Jago, Balai Pelestarian Kebudayaan Wilayah XI
sources.note: Official heritage account checked for Jajaghu, Wisnuwardhana's 1268 death, Kertanagara's patronage, and the 1268 to 1280 construction horizon. Scope: The temple's literary commemoration and later fabric are not collapsed into one exact building day.

sources.title: Al Haq and Wirasanti, Candi Keboireng: Aspek Keagamaan dan Kronologinya, AMERTA
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological article checked for the kala ornament, Mula Malurung reference, Kapulungan toponym, and Bhairawa worship in a Singhasari context. Scope: A site-specific religious interpretation does not define belief across East Java.

sources.title: Yusuf and Susilo, Reconstruction of the Bameswara Temple by Ken Angrok in Kediri, AMERTA
sources.note: Peer-reviewed 2025 study checked for two lintels dated 1148 Saka, the sparse record for Ken Angrok, and cautious reconstruction of political-religious consolidation in Kadiri. Scope: The authors' reconstruction is presented as an archaeological argument, not settled biography.

sources.title: Jan Wisseman Christie, The Development of Sawah Cultivation in Ancient Java
sources.note: University research checked for epigraphic terms for fields, seedbeds, barns, work animals, village organization, shared water, and cooperative labor. Scope: The study's broad ancient-Java reconstruction is not turned into one standard East Javanese village or timeless social personality.

sources.title: Jiri Jakl, Bhoma's Kitchen: Food Culture and Food Symbolism in Pre-Islamic Java
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article checked for twelfth-century Old Javanese descriptions of two-stage steamed rice, breakfast, dishes, feast food, and the symbolic character of literary evidence. Scope: Poetic dishes and elite feasts are not treated as an everyday menu for every household.

sources.title: Muhamad Satok Yusuf, Sumping Penanda Kesenian Arca pada Masa Kadiri-Singhasari
sources.note: Peer-reviewed art-history study checked for detailed ear ornaments, sculptural convention, artistic variation, and Kadiri-Singhasari style. Scope: Sacred sculpture and elite ornament are not treated as ordinary clothing photographs.

batchIdentityNotes: East Java is an atlas regional bucket, not one contemporary polity and not the modern Indonesian province.
The 1000 to 1279 interval crosses late Mataram or Isana, Airlangga or Kahuripan, Janggala, Panjalu or Kediri, and Singhasari histories.
The four-part polygon includes tested Central Java, southern Borneo, and Bima points while excluding tested Brantas-delta, north-coast, Madura, Bali, Lombok, and much of Sumbawa points.
The 1279 change to kediri is chronologically impossible: Kediri lost dominance in 1222 and Singhasari continued until 1292.
The endpoint is a map seam with cultural and community continuity. The override keeps fell null and supplies no false successor.
The Pucangan writing sample preserves scholarly transliteration and translation; original carved Kawi glyphs are explicitly absent because modern Unicode would not be a facsimile.
